This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

2. The brief case of the petitioner is as under:
On 24.02,2018 at about 03.30 pm.

When the petitioner was travelling in Auto rickshaw bg No.KA-40-A- 3975 along with other passengers on Gowribidanur towards vatada Hosahalli, in between Nakkhalli gate and Narasapura gate and on reaching near Eco Home (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.5262/2022 Asharama, Chikkaballapur District sustained grievous injuries as the driver of said Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA- 40-A-3975 driven the same in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed without following traffic rules dashed against the repaired auto rickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-40- A-405l on left side of the road and caused accident & injuries to petitioner.
The accident occurred due to sole rash & negligent driving of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 by its driver.
After the accident petitioner took treatment for one month at Victoria Hospital, Bangalore.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was working as a Cooking Bhattas and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries sustained by him he is unable to continue his avocation as earlier.
The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 by its driver.
The respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally are liable (SCCH-9) 4 MVC.No.5262/2022 to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
3. After service of summons, the respondent No.1 and the respondent No.2 have appeared through their respective counsel and respondent No.2 has filed its objections to the main petition.
4. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 is that, the claim petition is not maintainable in law or on facts of the same.

Further deposed that, the owner of the vehicle did not report and furnished the RTO documents pertaining to the offending Auto regarding the driving licence of the person who was driving the vehicle at the time of accident which required under Section 134(C) and the concerned police have not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.158(6)
of MV Act.
It has contented that, at the time of accident, the driver of the offending Auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 does not posses valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
It has contended that, the offending Auto (SCCH-9) 5 MVC.No.5262/2022 bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 in question did not hold valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.
It has denied the issuance of the policy in respect of Auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975.
Respondent No.2 has denied the involvement of the Auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 in the alleged accident.

Further contended that, the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner himself as the petitioner was negligently going in the vehicle which was filled with above the seating capacity and Venkatanarayana Rao vs Shanthakumar M.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117687756/
2 as such the vehicle lost control at the material time of the accident and contributed the accident.
The entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner to cause the accident.

Further contended that,
compensation claimed by the petitioner is exorbitant and fanciful.
With these grounds the respondent No.2 sought for rejecting the claim petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following issues:
 (SCCH-9) 6 MVC.No.5262/2022  ISSUES 1. Whether the petitioner prove that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 24.02.2018 at about 3.30 pm., near ECO Home Ashrema in between Nakkahalli Gate and Narasapura Gate, Chikkaballapura due to rash and negligent act of driving of Autorickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 by its driver as alleged in the petition ?

2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation? If so, what amount and from whom?
3.

What Order or Award?
6.

In order to prove his case, the petitioner himself examined as PW.1, one Medical Record Technician at Victoria Hospital has examined as PW.2 and Dr.S.Ramachandra has examined as PW.3 and in all got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P.13.

On the other hand, RTO,
Chikkaballapura has examined as RW.1 and Legal Manager, Shri Ram GIC Ltd., has examined as RW.2 and in all got marked Ex.R.1 to 4 and closed their side evidence.
Heard arguments and perused the materials available on record.

The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the following citations reported in :
1. (2018) 7 Supreme Court Cases 558 2. (2018) 8 Supreme Court Cases 492 3. MFA 101342 of 2017 8.

My answer to the above issues are as under:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative;
Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative; Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following:

9.

Issue No.1:- It is the case of the petitioner that, on 24.02,2018 at about 03.30 pm. When he was travelling in Auto rickshaw bg No.KA-40-A-3975 along with other passengers on Gowribidanur towards vatada Hosahalli, in between Nakkhalli gate and Narasapura gate and on reaching near Eco Home Asharama, Chikkaballapur District sustained grievous injuries as the driver of said (SCCH-9)
8 MVC.No.5262/2022 Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 driven the same in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed without following traffic rules dashed against the repaired auto rickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-405l on left side of the road.
Due to said impact he sustained grievous injuries.
10. In order to prove the case, the petitioner himself examined as PW1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief-examination and reiterated all the facts mentioned in the petition.
He also got marked Ex.P1 to P8 which are FIR, complaint, IMV report, spot panchanama, charge sheet, wound certificate, OPD slip and 2 X-rays.
11. I have perused police documents which are marked at Ex-P1 to Ex-P5.

From these documents it is clear that the accident took place on 24.02.2018 at about 3.30 pm., and Ex.P.1 - FIR in crime No.0056/2018 came to be registered on 24.02.2018 at 19.15 i.e., on the same day of accident at Gowribidanur Police Station for the (SCCH-9) 9 MVC.No.5262/2022 offences punishable u/s 279,
337 of IPC.
Ex. P.2
- complaint lodged by petitioner himself on 24.02.2018.

Ex.P.3 is the IMV report which discloses that, vehicle bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 got damages like rear left side center body damaged, rear left side chassis damaged and for vehicle bearing No.KA-40-A-4051 got damages like rear right side corner body damaged.

Ex.P.4 is the spot panchanama which denoted the spot of accident as towards east - Ramanjanappa land, towards west - ECO Home Ashrama, towards North - Nakkalahalli gate to Hosahalli road and towards South - road from Narasapura to Gowribidanur.

Ex.P.5 is the charge sheet which was registered against driver of the offending Auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 for the offences punishable under Section 181, 3 of MV Act and 337, 279, 338 of IPC.
12.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has cross examined PW-1.
I have perused the entire cross- examination of PW-1.

In his cross-examination he has (SCCH-9) 10 MVC.No.5262/2022 specifically denied the suggestions made by the learned counsel for the respondent regarding, by his own negligence the alleged accident occurred.
The learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has not elicited anything from the mouth of PW-1 to disbelieve his version.
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law

that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, on over all appreciation of evidence, I am of the opinion that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence of driver of the offending Auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 which belongs to the respondent No.1 and respondent No.2 is its insurer.

4 (SCCH-9) 11 MVC.No.5262/2022 Accordingly, I answer issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering Issue No.1 in the affirmative the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation the Tribunal has to look into several facts like injuries,
pain and suffering, sustained by the petitioner and amount spent by the petitioner towards medical expenses, food and extra nourishment, medical and attendant charges, conveyance, loss of income during treatment, disability, loss of amenities etc.
let me discuss one by one:
a) Towards Injury, Pain and Suffering:
The petitioner has contended due to accident he was sustained Type 3B open fracture (L) femur, fracture of shaft of femur distal 3rd and IT and all over the body.
He underwent operation for the said fractures at Victoria Hospital.

In order to prove injuries caused to him, he has produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P6 which reveals that petitioner has sustained open fracture left femur and (SCCH-9) 12 MVC.No.5262/2022 intertrochanteric fracture and treatment done for CRIF with long PFN and SA3 on 05.03.2018 and doctor opined that the said mentioned injury is grievious in nature and fresh.
Further, Petitioner examined one Medical Record Technician as PW.2 and got marked Authrosiation letter, MLC records and inpatient record at Ex.
Petitioner has also examined Dr. S.Ramachandra as PW.3 and got marked outpatient record at Ex.P.11, Hospital receipt at Ex.P.12 and X-ray marked at Ex.P.13.
PW.3 has assessed the disability of petitioner.
Therefore by considering the injury and facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that the compensation of Rs.50,000/- is just and reasonable towards pain and sufferings.
b) Towards Medical Expenses: PW.1 has contended that, he undergone operations/treatment for the said fractures at Victoria Hospital.
He was inpatient in the said hospital for four weeks and spent Rs.5,00,000/- fore (SCCH-9) 13 MVC.No.5262/2022 treatment, conveyance and lost the bills.
Therefore, by considering the same, it is just and reasonable to award Rs.5,000/- under the head Medical expenses.

c) Towards food, extra nourishment, Conveyance and medical attendant charges: PW.1 has deposed that, immediately after accident he took treatment at Government Hospital, Gowribidanur and then shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bangalore wherein he took treatment as an inpatient.
In proof of the same, petitioner has not produced discharge summary.
But on perusal of Ex.P.9 - MLC records it came know that, petitioner took treatment as an inpatient from 25.02.2018 to 19.03.2018 i.e., for 23 days.

Considering the said fact the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.1,000/- per day for 23 days and by including expenses of attendant of petitioner during the period of treatment and also by including conveyance, in all a sum of Rs.30,000/- is just and reasonable towards food extra (SCCH-9) 14 MVC.No.5262/2022 nourishment, conveyance and medical attendant charges.

d) Towards Loss of Income during treatment:

sentences.text: The petitioner contended that he was working as Cook and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.

Therefore, in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.

Accordingly, the fixed notional income of the year 2018 at Rs.12,500/- p.m.,
Petitioner may took 3 months rest and he may lost income for those rest periods.
Therefore, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is entitled to Rs.37,500/- (Rs.12,500/- x 3) towards loss of income during treatment period.
e) Towards Future Earnings:
The petitioner has contended that due to accident he was inpatient in the (SCCH-9) 15 MVC.No.5262/2022 hospital and has become permanently disabled.

The petitioner also examined Dr.S.Ramachandra working as Senior Consultant and DNB P G Teacher at General Hospital, Jayanager as PW.3 and through got marked Ex.P.11 - out patient record, Ex.P.12 - Hospital receipt and Ex.P.13 -X-ray.

PW.3 has contended that, petitioner was diagnosed to have Type III 'B'
open (compound) fracture shaft of left femur and intertrochanteric fracture left femur.
Further petitioner underwent CRIF with long PFN done on 05.03.2018 and discharged on 19.03.2018.
For the purpose of disability assessment he examined the petitioner on 19.02.2024.

PW.3 assessed that,
the petitioner suffered the permanent residual physical disability of about 38.99% of left lower limb which is about 19.44% of whole body.
During cross examination
PW.3 has deposed that, he has no treated the petitioner and not collected any written information from treated doctor.
Further deposed that, (SCCH-9) 16 MVC.No.5262/2022 implants is still in situ, fractures are united.
Further he has admitted that, the patient would have remove the implant and petitioner can do agricultural and coolie work with difficulty.
It is relevant to note that according to PW.3 has assessed permanent residual physical disability of about 38.99% of left lower limb which is about 19.44% of whole body.

It is well settled law that it is the impact of the physical disability on the particular avocation of the petitioner which is relevant for the purpose of assessment of compensation under the head of loss of future income as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in Rajkumar's case reported in (2011) 1 SCC 343.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.3 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 15% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.

As per unmarked Aadhar card and as per the medical (SCCH-9) 17 MVC.No.5262/2022 records,
petitioner was aged about 53 to 54 years as on the date of accident.

Under such circumstances, the age of petitioner was considered in the age group of 51 to 55 years and same is taken into consideration for applying multiplier and the proper multiplier is "11" is applicable as per Smt.Sarala Verma's case.

Hence future earning capacity of the petitioner due to permanent disability works out as under:
12,500 x 12 x 11 x 15% = Rs.2,47,500/-
Venkatanarayana Rao vs Shanthakumar M.N on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/117687756/
6

Therefore, the petitioner is entitled Rs.2,47,500/-
under the head of loss of future earning capacity.

f) Towards deprivation of Future Amenities:
The doctor has opined that the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and he is unable do his day to day activities as earlier.
By considering the facts and circumstances of the case the Tribunal is of the view that compensation of Rs.10,000/- is just and reasonable to under the head of deprivation of future amenities.

Towards future medical expenses: PW.3 has deposed that, petitioner is advised to undergo another operation for removal of implants from left femur which would cost around Rs.50,000/- in private set up.
Therefore, petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/- under the head future medical expenses which shall not carry any interest.
14. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as follows:

The respondent No.2 has taken contention that, as on the date of accident the driver of offending auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 was not holding valid and effective driving licence.

Further it is the contention of the respondent No.2 that, the offending auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 in question did not hold valid permit and FC as on the date of accident.
In support of it, Insurance company has examined its Legal Manager as RW.2 and through her got marked authorisation letter at Ex.R.3, insurance policy at Ex.R.4.

But during cross examination of RW.1 by the learned counsel for petitioner has admitted that,  
..2      . On perusal of Ex.R.2 it came to know that, the vehicle bearing reg.No.KA- 40-A-3975 is having validity of the permit from 16.09.2022 to 15.09.2027.
It shows that, there is gross violation of policy condition by the owner of the offending auto bearing reg.No.KA-40-A-3975 as the offending vehicle not having valid permit as on the date of accident.

The learned counsel for petitioner has relied upon the citation reported in:

On perusal of above said discussion at citations it came to be know that, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the Insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2 Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner at the (SCCH-9) 28 MVC.No.5262/2022 first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.1.

The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order and the petitioner is entitled for 6% interest on the compensation amount of .3,90,000/- from the date of petition till realisation.
Hence, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:

For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .3,90,000/- (Rupees three lakhs ninety thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(Future medical expenses shall not carry any interest)
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the (SCCH-9) 29 MVC.No.5262/2022 petitioner.
The respondent No.2 - Insurer shall pay the compensation amount with interest at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.1 - Owner.
The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.
When the petitioner was travelling in Auto rickshaw bg No.KA-40-A- 3975 along with other passengers on Gowribidanur towards vatada Hosahalli, in between Nakkhalli gate and Narasapura gate and on reaching near Eco Home (SCCH-9) 3 MVC.No.5262/2022 Asharama, Chikkaballapur District sustained grievous injuries as the driver of said Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA- 40-A-3975 driven the same in rash and negligent manner with excessive speed without following traffic rules dashed against the repaired auto rickshaw bearing reg.No.KA-40- A-405l on left side of the road and caused accident & injuries to petitioner.
The accident occurred due to sole rash & negligent driving of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 by its driver.
Prior to the accident, the petitioner was working as a Cooking Bhattas and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries sustained by him he is unable to continue his avocation as earlier.
The accident occurred solely due to the rash and negligent driving of the Auto rickshaw bearing No.KA-40-A-3975 by its driver.
The entire negligence is on the part of the petitioner to cause the accident.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
There is nothing on record to show that the charge-sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
Moreover, it is settled law
that the term "rashness and negligence" has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the MV Act as compare to the word "rashness and negligence" as finds mention in the Indian Penal Code.
This is because the provisions of M.V.Act dealing with compensation are benevolent legislation and not a penal one.
Therefore, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case the petitioner is entitled to Rs.37,500/- (Rs.12,500/- x 3) towards loss of income during treatment period.
By looking into the record it seems that PW.3 has assessed disability of the Petitioner at higher side.
Therefore, the Petitioner might be having 15% disability to the whole body which cannot be ruled out.

also in the citation reported in 2020 ACJ 2560 (New India Assurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Yallavva and another) wherein it is held that:

On perusal of above said discussion at citations it came to be know that, the compensation determined must be first paid by the insurer, who could thereafter recover the same from the owner of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner and the respondent No.2 being the Insurer are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fixed on the respondent No.2 Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the compensation amount with interest to the petitioner at the (SCCH-9) 28 MVC.No.5262/2022 first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.1.

16. Issue No.3:
For the forgoing reasons and in view of above discussion, Tribunal proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for total compensation amount of .3,90,000/- (Rupees three lakhs ninety thousand only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realization.
(Future medical expenses shall not carry any interest)
The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the (SCCH-9) 29 MVC.No.5262/2022 petitioner.
The respondent No.2 - Insurer shall pay the compensation amount with interest at the first instance and recover the same from the respondent No.1 - Owner.
The respondent No.2 is directed to pay the compensation amount within two months from the date of this order.
In the event of deposit of the said compensation amount, 25% shall be deposited in the name of petitioner for a period of 3 years in Karnataka Bank, City Civil Court Branch, Bengaluru and the remaining 75% shall be released in favour of petitioner on proper identification through e-payment.
Advocate fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
